prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1489; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a low-speed collision in the parking lot of a retail center. Insured vehicle reported as struck by a second vehicle while reversing. Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness following the impact and has been advised to seek medical evaluation. Claimant is not represented by counsel at this time.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant describes whiplash-type symptoms, including neck stiffness and headache, beginning the day after the collision. Claimant states they have scheduled a visit with their primary care provider. Explained the claims process and the documentation needed, including medical records and itemized bills. Claimant has no attorney and says they would like to handle the matter directly.

Entry 3: Photos of both vehicles received from the claimant and the insured. Damage to the rear bumper of the claimant's vehicle is consistent with a low-speed impact. Scene diagram obtained from the insured shows the vehicles' positions and direction of travel. No police report was filed because no authority responded to the scene.

Entry 4: Received medical authorization form from claimant. Claimant reports ongoing neck pain and reduced range of motion, with physical therapy recommended by treating provider. Reviewed the treatment plan with claimant and noted that the claim file will be updated once records arrive. Claimant continues to indicate no legal representation.

Entry 5: Medical records received and under review. Diagnosis listed as cervical strain consistent with whiplash. Treatment to date includes physical therapy sessions and prescribed muscle relaxants. Claim remains open pending receipt of itemized medical bills and the independent review of the injury. Follow-up call scheduled with claimant to confirm status of treatment.
